title: A regular immersion of smooth schemes over a perfect field
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a regular closed immersion of pure codimension
$c$, with $X$ smooth over the perfect field $k$ and $Z$ regular and locally
of finite type over $k$. Then both structure morphisms $a_X:X\to\Spec k$ and
$a_Z=a_X\circ i:Z\to\Spec k$ are smooth, and for every point $z\in Z$
$$\dim\mathcal O_{X,i(z)}=\dim\mathcal O_{Z,z}+c.$$

proof.text: By hypothesis $a_X$ is smooth. Regard $Z$ as a $k$-scheme with structure morphism $a_Z=a_X\circ i$; this is precisely the composition required for a morphism of $k$-schemes by [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Thus the claimed identity of structure morphisms is definitional.

source.place: First and last sentences; structure-morphism identity

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-regular-perfect-field-smooth] to $a_Z:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its three hypotheses are exactly the perfectness of $k$, the assumed regularity of $Z$, and the assumed local finite type of $a_Z$. It gives smoothness of $a_Z$. This criterion is the equality of the regular and smooth loci over a perfect field (Stacks Tag 0B8X); it requires neither connectedness nor quasi-compactness.

source.place: Tag 0B8X, lemma-dense-smooth-open-variety-over-perfect-field; equality of the two loci

proof.text: Fix $z\in Z$ and put $x=i(z)$. The regular-immersion convention of [sk-def-purity-conv] supplies an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$ on which the defining ideal is $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$, with $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ an $A$-regular sequence. This condition is needed only near points of $Z$, and allows $c=0$. By the affine description of [def-weil-closed-immersion], $i^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ over $U$. Write $\mathfrak q$ for the prime of $A/J$ corresponding to $z$, and $\mathfrak p$ for its inverse image in $A$, so $J\subseteq\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $R:=\mathcal O_{X,x}\cong A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $S:=\mathcal O_{Z,z}\cong(A/J)_{\mathfrak q}$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] identifies $S$ with $A_{\mathfrak p}/JA_{\mathfrak p}$ by the explicit map $\overline{a/s}\mapsto\bar a/\bar s$.

source.place: Tag 00CT, proposition-localize-quotient; affine closed immersion Tag 01QO (morphisms.tex), stalk localization Tag 01HV (schemes.tex)

proof.text: Since $a_X$ is smooth, [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] makes every local ring of $X$ regular; in particular $R$ is a Noetherian local ring. Each $f_j$ belongs to $J\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-regular-sequence-localization-prime] to $A$, $\mathfrak p$ and the chosen sequence: its image $f_1/1,\ldots,f_c/1$ is an $A_{\mathfrak p}$-regular sequence. The required weak regularity follows from the regular sequence chosen in step 3. This also covers the empty sequence; the local ring at a point is nonzero.

source.place: Tag 056S, lemma-smooth-regular; localization of a regular sequence as in algebra.tex Tag 00LF (definition-regular-sequence), via localization exactness

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-regular-sequence-dimension-formula] to the Noetherian local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ and the length-$c$ regular sequence from step 4. It gives $\dim(A_{\mathfrak p}/(f_1/1,\ldots,f_c/1))+c=\dim A_{\mathfrak p}$. The ideal in this quotient is $JA_{\mathfrak p}$: an element generated by the $f_j/1$ is a fraction with numerator in $J$, and every $a/s$ with $a\in J$ is such a linear combination after dividing its coefficients by $s$. Step 3 identifies the two rings with $S$ and $R$. Ring isomorphisms preserve Krull dimension because inverse images and images give inverse order-preserving bijections of their prime ideals and of chains of prime ideals. Hence $\dim\mathcal O_{X,i(z)}=\dim\mathcal O_{Z,z}+c$. The argument holds for every $z$; if $Z$ is empty the dimension assertion is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 00KW, lemma-one-equation, iterated along a regular sequence; exact existing Mathlib leaf ringKrullDim_add_length_eq_ringKrullDim_of_isRegular
